ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal Act on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing of 10 October 1997 (AMLA, SR 955.0), current version; Swiss Criminal Code (SR 311.0), Arts. 305bis-305quater; Swiss Code of Obligations (SR 220), Arts. 626 et seq. and 717a (registered beneficial ownership); Ordinance on the Register of Beneficial Owners of Companies and Legal Entities (SR 221.956.1); Federal Act on the Adaptation of Legal Entities to the Revised Transparency Requirements (2019/2021). The statutory UBO filing is directed to the Federal Office of Justice and retained in the registered office documentation.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport and proof of residential address for each shareholder, director and beneficial owner of 25% or more
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority / communal civil registry of the shareholder's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille where issued in a Hague Convention state; otherwise consular legalization by the Swiss representation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing or certificate of incorporation of any corporate shareholder holding 25% or more of the Swiss AG
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial register authority / official company registry of the foreign shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the foreign registry, followed by notarized Swiss translation where required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Duly signed and notarized power of attorney for incorporation submitted by non-resident founders or attorneys-in-fact
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the jurisdiction of execution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization for non-Hague jurisdictions) and, where necessary, sworn translation into German, French or Italian

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders and UBOs against the consolidated SECO sanctions list (State Secretariat for Economic Affairs), UN Security Council sanctions in force for Switzerland, EU autonomous sanctions as adopted by Switzerland, and Swiss Federal Criminal Police databases. Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) are subjected to enhanced due diligence in accordance with AMLA Arts. 3, 6 and 6a, and FINMA Circular 2020/1, including PEP residence and family-member analysis. OFAC and OFSI listings are additionally checked as a prudent best-practice measure for non-Swiss payment rails in USD/GBP.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix (www.zefix.ch), the official central index of the Swiss commercial register, managed in coordination with the competent Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt / Office du registre du commerce).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name may appear only in Latin characters in the official Swiss commercial register; any non-Latin character name must be transliterated in the registered linguistic form of the canton of the registered office. The legal form suffix must be expressed in the official Swiss language of the seat canton: 'Aktiengesellschaft (AG)' in the German-speaking region, 'Société anonyme (SA)' in the French-speaking region, and 'Società anonima (SA)' in the Italian-speaking region. Foreign words are permitted only if written in Latin letters and if they do not mislead economic circles under Arts. 950-951 of the Swiss Code of Obligations.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: In the event of a negative name-clearance decision, the Cantonal Commercial Register Office must furnish written grounds. The applicant may submit a written reconsideration request to the same office within 10 days, addressing the misleading-character objection or providing an alternative transliteration/name variant. If reconsideration is denied, a formal administrative appeal must be filed with the competent Cantonal Administrative Court within 30 days of notification, invoking Arts. 950-956c of the Swiss Code of Obligations. A further appeal on questions of federal law lies to the Swiss Federal Supreme Court in Lausanne within 30 days after the cantonal decision.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Limited virtual-office permissibility. A Swiss AG may be registered at a domiciliation address only where a licensed commercial domiciliation provider maintains a physical office at that address, mail forwarding and service-of-process support, and statutory corporate records remain accessible in Switzerland. A strict virtual mailbox with no Swiss business address, no local agent and no document availability is not acceptable for a registered Swiss Aktiengesellschaft.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low quantified risk, estimated at approximately 3-5% per year for a low-risk audio-dubbing/post-production business using a licensed domiciliation provider. The risk increases to 15-25% in the presence of Swiss VAT refund claims, payroll tax registration, suspicious UBO filing inconsistencies, or tax-authority substance audits; unannounced inspections are materially more likely where the domiciliation provider serves a high volume of letterbox companies.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht, OR), Arts. 620–659 and 716a et seq.; Commercial Register Ordinance (Handelsregisterverordnung, HRegV), Arts. 72–100.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized deed of incorporation (öffentliche Beurkundung) and application for entry in the Commercial Register (Anmeldung zur Eintragung ins Handelsregister)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum fully subscribed share capital is CHF 100,000. At incorporation, at least 20% of the nominal value of each share must be paid in, being not less than CHF 50,000 in aggregate. Paid-up capital must be deposited in a Swiss blocked bank account and released only after provisional registration with the Commercial Register; the bank must deliver a release declaration (Freigabeerklärung).
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The Board of Directors of the newly formed Aktiengesellschaft hereby: (1) confirms the subscription and allotment of 1,000 registered shares with a nominal value of CHF 100 each, constituting the full share capital of CHF 100,000; (2) adopts the registered office at the address stated in the articles of association in Zug, Switzerland; (3) appoints [Given Name] [Family Name] as President and [Given Name] [Family Name] as Secretary and Legal Representative; (4) approves the opening of a corporate bank account and the release of the blocked paid-up capital upon Commercial Register registration; (5) instructs the filing of the incorporation application with the Commercial Register; and (6) authorizes each officer to execute ancillary declarations, including tax forms and permit applications, in the name of the company.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Notarize Articles of Association (Statuten)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Notary Public, Canton of Zug (öffentliche Beurkundung)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the articles of association before the notary, confirming company name, registered office, share capital, share classes, board composition, and permitted purpose (AI subtitle transcription and voice dubbing studio). The deed must expressly declare the full subscription of all shares and the amount of paid-up capital.
required_dossiers: Valid passport or Swiss identity document of each founder or shareholder
Draft articles of association in German
Company name availability certificate from the Commercial Register (ZGB/HR name search)
Declaration of share subscriptions and board elections
Bank confirmation of paid-up capital if the blocked capital account has been opened
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name or notarial deed is queried, file an amended deed or a curative declaration with the same notary within 10 days and re-submit for notarization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Blocked Capital Deposit Account and Pay Up Share Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: FINMA-licensed Swiss bank in Zug or a cantonal bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked capital account in the proposed company name, deposit at least CHF 50,000 in paid-up capital, and obtain the bank's release declaration (Freigabeerklärung) confirming that the funds are at the free disposal of the incorporation applicants, subject solely to release upon Commercial Register registration.
required_dossiers: Draft articles of association
Notarized deed excerpt
Passport or Swiss ID of each authorized board member
Proof of residence or domicile of board members
Completed bank client onboarding and KYC/AML forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank raises KYC queries, provide updated source-of-funds documentation or transfer the account to another FINMA-licensed bank without restarting the notarial procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Commercial Register Application and Publish Notice
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug (Commercial Register Office of Canton Zug)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized deed, board appointment consents, bank capital declaration, specimen signature cards, and application form to the Commercial Register. The registry performs statutory compliance review and, upon approval, arranges publication in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB).
required_dossiers: Notarized deed of incorporation
Bank release declaration for paid-up capital
Board appointment consents and signed signature cards
Commercial Register application form (Anmeldung)
Domicile declaration for the registered office if required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond in writing to any requisition within the official deadline and provide corrected documents; if the application is rejected, amend the deed and re-file expeditiously.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Company Identification Number (UID) and VAT Status
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Federal Statistical Office (BFS) and Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/ATA), automatic after commercial register entry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon registration, the company is automatically allocated a Swiss company identification number (UID). Review the SHAB entry and order a certified Commercial Register excerpt. Register for VAT if taxable turnover is expected to exceed CHF 100,000 per year; otherwise maintain non-registered status until the threshold applies.
required_dossiers: Certified Commercial Register excerpt
Company details and projected turnover statement
Passport copies of board members and beneficial owners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the UID or VAT status is incorrect, request a correction through the federal UID portal or the competent ESTV tax office using the registered company data.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Activate Corporate Governance Records and Bank Mandates
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors with notification to the Cantonal Commercial Register where required
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold and minute the first board meeting adopting the statutory share register (Aktienbuch) and establishing the required corporate record books: shareholders ledger, board minutes, and contracts register. After provisional registration, update the bank signature cards to the final authorized board signatories and obtain the release of blocked capital from the deposit bank.
required_dossiers: Certified Commercial Register excerpt
Original specimen signature cards
Share register template
Board resolution for bank mandate changes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses the mandate update, provide an updated certified register excerpt and re-execute the signature cards with the company secretary.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Canton Zug Department of Economic Affairs (Amt für Wirtschaft und Arbeit) and the municipal building authority (Baudepartment Zug)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal commercial operation license (Betriebsbewilligung) and building occupancy permit (Gebrauchsbewilligung) for a sound studio and office premises

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (BAFU/FOEN) and Canton Zug Department for Environment (IfU)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from formal environmental impact assessment under the Swiss Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (UVPV, Anhang); subject to general permitting and low-emission operating rules for audio post-production activities.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater discharge from subtitle or dubbing operations; noise emissions from HVAC and studio equipment must comply with cantonal noise abatement limits under the Noise Protection Ordinance (LSV); waste electrical and electronic equipment must be disposed through SWICO/SENS-certified recyclers; airborne emissions, if any, must comply with Ordinance on Air Pollution Control (LRV).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification and fire prevention clearance under VKF cantonal fire safety standards, including alarms, egress, and extinguishers; structural load inspection prior to studio equipment installation; occupational health and safety clearance by SUVA under the Swiss Labor Law (ArG) and SECO workplace guidelines, including hearing protection and ergonomic standards.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung ESTV / Administration fédérale des contributions AFC / Amministrazione federale delle contribuzioni AFC), Federal Department of Finance; central portal: https://www.estv.admin.ch; company registration database: https://www.zefix.ch; UID register: https://www.uid.admin.ch. Cantonal and communal tax administrations levy separate corporate income/capital taxes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Swiss AG obtains its statutory business identification number (UID, equivalent to the Swiss TIN) automatically upon inscription in the Commercial Register (Handelsregister) through the cantonal register office; the UID is displayed in Zefix. For Swiss VAT, the AG must file a VAT registration application with the ESTV's Register of Value Added Tax via the FTA e-portal within 30 days of commencing or exceeding the CHF 100,000 taxable-turnover threshold; the ESTV assigns a VAT number in the format CHE-123.456.789 MWST. Foreign entities without a Swiss registered seat that perform taxable supplies in Switzerland (e.g., AI subtitle/audio services to Swiss business customers) must obtain a UID from the ESTV for VAT purposes, file through the same electronic procedure, and, absent a Swiss branch or establishment, appoint a Swiss fiscal representative who is jointly liable for VAT.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (Swiss AG is a resident corporate taxpayer subject to federal, cantonal and communal profit and capital taxes; no domestic pass-through or check-the-box classification is available; Swiss tax law applies a modified territoriality principle, exempting foreign permanent-establishment profits and foreign real property from Swiss corporate income tax while retaining progression).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election exists. Elective mechanisms available: (i) VAT grouping for closely integrated companies (economic, organisational and financial integration with direct/indirect majority control) to be treated as a single taxable person; (ii) Swiss group taxation election for direct-tax purposes (Steuergruppe) allowing a controlling Swiss parent and its majority-held Swiss subsidiaries to file as a consolidated taxpayer; (iii) STAF incentive elections (patent box, R&D super-deduction, notional interest deduction) applied for with the competent cantonal tax authority; (iv) voluntary VAT registration option for below-threshold taxpayers, enabling input-tax recovery. Hybrid mismatch treatment is non-elective: Swiss law applies mandatory anti-hybrid rules recharacterizing payments under blended arrangements; foreign entity classifications do not bind the Swiss tax administration.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (Schweizerische Nationalbank / Banca Nazionale Svizzera) as the monetary and currency-issuing authority; no separate foreign-exchange administration exists. Prudential supervision of banks and payment institutions is exercised by the Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority (FINMA), and tax/double-taxation treaty policy by the State Secretariat for International Finance (SIF).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland provides full, unrestricted convertibility on both current-account and capital-account transactions. There is no foreign-exchange control law, no requirement to obtain permission for opening or operating foreign-currency accounts, and no restriction on the repatriation of profits, dividends, loan repayments, or capital wind-up proceeds. The only fiscal friction on shareholder profit remittance is the standard 35% Swiss anticipatory withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) on dividends; this may be reduced or fully refunded under an applicable double-taxation treaty or where the recipient is a Swiss beneficial owner, and it constitutes a fiscal cost rather than an exchange-convertibility barrier. Foreign-ownership of a Swiss AG is unrestricted, and the Swiss franc is freely tradable in spot, forward, and swap markets. Therefore, profit remittance hurdles are negligible; treasury planning should focus on treaty eligibility, substance, and documentary support for reduced withholding rates.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Switzerland does not impose any statutory timeline for export-receipt repatriation, no mandatory conversion ratio of export proceeds into CHF, and no surrender or escrow regime for export earnings. A Swiss AG may retain invoiced proceeds in original foreign currency in any Swiss or foreign account, convert at its own discretion, and settle commercial obligations in any currency. As internal treasury best practice, a notional conversion of export receipts into CHF within 30 days of receipt is recommended to minimise accounting FX volatility, but this is not a legal obligation.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Corporate Account in CHF/EUR/USD; Capital-Contribution Escrow Sub-Account used for notarial incorporation
Operational Current Account; Capital Escrow Account
Operational Account and Merchant Settlement Account for e-commerce and payment-rail sweeps
Treasury and Corporate Payments Account; Wealth/Corporate Pairing

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Raiffeisen Schweiz Genossenschaft (St. Gallen / regional offices)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: HIGH for Wise (Wise Payments AG, Zug, holding a FINMA fintech licence under Art. 1b of the Swiss Banking Act, with Swiss IBAN issuance) and for Stripe (Stripe Technology Europe Ltd acting under the Swiss correspondent/fintech umbrella via local merchant accounts). MEDIUM for offshore challenger EMIs such as Airwallex, Revolut Business, and Payoneer, which may on-board the Swiss AG but typically issue only foreign IBANs (GB/LT/IE) and do not constitute a replacement for a regulated Swiss bank account. Legal constraint: Swiss law (Banking Act Art. 1) requires a banking licence for any entity professionally accepting deposit-like funds from the public in Switzerland; an offshore EMI rendering deposit or payment services into Switzerland without FINMA authorisation violates Swiss regulatory law and exposes the treasury to compliance cascading risk. Therefore the AG must maintain its primary liquidity and statutory capital in a FINMA-licensed Swiss bank or Swiss branch; EMIs are permitted as collection/aggregation endpoints (Stripe/Wise) subject to mandatory daily sweeps into the Swiss bank account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote account opening is legally permitted for low-risk, non-US, clean-AML Swiss AGs using FINMA-compliant video identification (AVD) in accordance with FINMA Anti-Money Laundering Ordinance and FINMA Circular 2016/07 (recorded video call with a certified identification provider). In practice, most Tier-1 Swiss banks require a physical or near-physical interview at some stage: a personal appearance of at least one authorised signatory or UBO at the Swiss branch, or a personal appearance before a notary of the bank's correspondent network. For directors who cannot travel, banks usually accept a bundle comprising: (i) certified copy of passport and apostilled Swiss Commercial Register extract (Handelsregisterauszug), (ii) video/KYC interview with the bank's compliance officer, and (iii) notarised powers of attorney for local representatives. A mandatory physical-interview escalation applies where any director or UBO is a politically exposed person, resident in a high-risk FATF grey-list jurisdiction, or where the initial share-capital remittance exceeds CHF 50,000 from a non-FATF-white-list jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO or director tax residence in a high-risk or non-FATF-compliant jurisdiction; opaque multi-tier UBO chain; PEP involvement.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled Swiss Commercial Register (Handelsregisterauszug) for the AG; notarised identity documents and proof of address of every director/shareholder; complete Form A/Annex I UBO declaration under the Swiss Anti-Money Laundering Ordinance; individual tax-residence certificates from the relevant jurisdictions; sworn source-of-wealth statement; independent legal-opinion letter from a Swiss attorney confirming the absence of beneficial-ownership concealment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial share-capital contribution (CHF 100,000 nominal, minimum CHF 50,000 paid-in) originated from a crypto exchange, an unregulated EMI, or a third-country private account.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank-statement chain evidencing the exact source of funds from a regulated financial institution; exchange KYC certificate and trade/transaction history from the crypto platform; notarial deed of incorporation confirming the capital contribution (Liberation du Capital); certified translation of the contributor's banker's reference letter; signed undertaking that the funds are solely for working capital; sworn statement that funds are not derived from proceeds of crime.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Automatic subtitle transcription and AI voice-cloning business flagged by compliance as high-risk technology for fraud, deep-fake, or intellectual-property-infringement exposure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed business plan and executed client contracts demonstrating lawful post-production use; source-code ownership deeds and IP assignment register; ISIC 5912/NAICS 512191 classification certificate; Swiss data-protection compliance statement (revised FADP/GDPR alignment) demonstrating lawful processing of voices and subtitles; representational warranty that services are not used for political disinformation or market manipulation; relevant professional-liability insurance certificate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Lack of economic substance; perceived shell structure holding funds for non-resident founders.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Lease agreement for physical Swiss registered office (Zug/Zürich area); Swiss payroll records and social-security (AHV) contribution statements for local staff; board-meeting minutes physically held in Switzerland; Swiss corporate tax/VAT receipts; audit or accounting firm engagement letter; active trade records (commercial invoices, receipts, platform payouts) demonstrating genuine AI dubbing and subtitling activity.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing: foreign shareholder transfers at least CHF 50,000 (the statutory paid-in portion for CHF 100,000 nominal capital) via SWIFT MT103 to the bank's notarial escrow sub-account opened in the company's name before incorporation; the bank requires a copy of the notarised deed of incorporation and a board resolution designating the operational account; the purpose narrative must explicitly state 'share capital contribution according to notarial deed' and the bank maps it to an appropriate ISO 20022 purpose code (e.g., 'COMC' or 'INVS') for statistical/AML classification. If the transfer originates from an EMI or crypto wallet, a complete source-of-funds verification package must accompany the instruction; remittance address and order must match the contributor's documented KYC profile. Post-incorporation operating inflows from overseas sales are tagged with the invoice reference and service description, avoiding any confusion with capital increases; any subsequent capital increase above CHF 100,000 nominal requires a notarial deed and Commercial Register registration before the transfer can be received.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails: (i) SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfers and MT202 cover payments for direct CHF/EUR/USD/GBP supplier and licensor outpayments; (ii) SIC (Swiss Interbank Clearing) for CHF domestic and cross-border CHF settlement; (iii) EURO-SIC and SEPA Credit Transfer via Swiss bridge interfaces for EUR-denominated trade within SEPA; (iv) commercial letters of credit (documentary credits under UCP 600) advised/confirmed by the Swiss relationship bank for high-value co-production milestone payments and IP acquisitions; (v) card and payment-facilitator rails (Stripe/Wise) for micro-transactions, subject to daily sweeps to the Swiss treasury account. Each outbound instruction must attach the supporting invoice/contract and be classified with SWIFT purpose/transaction codes such as 'ROYL' for software royalties, 'SERV' for media production services, and 'LIC' for licensing fees. The treasury policy requires that all disbursements be executed from the FINMA-licensed Swiss bank account and prohibits settlement directly from an offshore EMI account, preserving audit clarity and reducing AML friction.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX Spot transactions for immediate conversion between CHF, EUR, USD, GBP and other freely convertible currencies with the Swiss relationship bank
Outright FX Forwards on liquid currencies (EUR/USD/GBP/JPY) executed under a standard ISDA or Swiss Master Agreement for hedging forecast trade receivables/payables

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) on restricted emerging-market currencies (offshore CNY/CNH, INR, KRW, and certain Latin American currencies) to hedge localization revenue where onshore convertibility is limited
Cross-Currency Swaps (fixed-to-floating and floating-to-fixed) for medium-term hedging of multi-year dubbing/subtitling subscription flows and cost bases
FX Options and zero-premium collars (tunnel forwards) purchased OTC from a FINMA-regulated Swiss bank, providing budget certainty on long-term USD/EUR revenue streams without upfront premium cost
Short-term currency swaps with the Swiss clearing bank for temporary liquidity matching in different settlement currencies

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting approval of annual financial statements and auditor appointment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Not a government filing; shareholders’ resolution recorded in Minute Book and retained on site
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the balance-sheet date under Article 640 CO; for a calendar-year company, no later than 30 June of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors may be held jointly liable; shareholders may request a court-convened meeting; no administrative strike-off is triggered solely by late AGM approval

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements and audit report filing (only for AGs subject to ordinary statutory audit)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months after the balance-sheet date, following approval by the Annual General Meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Commercial Register may issue a reminder and impose a coercive fine; persistent non-filing may trigger the official administrative strike-off procedure under Article 935a CO after formal notice

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax and cantonal net wealth tax return (covers federal direct tax and cantonal/communal taxes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Administration; Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA) for federal direct tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally no later than 30 June of the following tax year for calendar-year companies; extension to September or October is customary at cantonal discretion
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest, late-filing penalty, summary assessment on non-compliance; tax evasion penalties up to one-third or more of the evaded tax may be levied; no direct administrative strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Swiss VAT return (for AGs using annual reporting frequency)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the close of the VAT reporting period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest, maintenance charge, administrative fine up to one-third of the evaded tax, and criminal penalty for intentional concealment; no strike-off is triggered

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial Register mutation filings (changes to directors, share capital, registered office, corporate purpose, or shareholders triggering register updates)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 14 days after the change; if no corporate change occurs, no annual filing is required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to CHF 5,000 may be imposed on responsible officers; after repeated formal notices, the Commercial Register may strike off the AG under the administrative deregistration procedure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual franchise tax or business licence renewal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Not applicable — Switzerland does not impose a general franchise tax or annual business licence renewal on AGs

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An ordinary audit is mandatory if the AG exceeds any two of the following thresholds for two consecutive financial years: balance-sheet total above CHF 20 million; total annual revenue above CHF 40 million; annual average of 250 full-time employees. Listed and regulated AGs are always subject to ordinary audit. A limited audit is required for other AGs unless all shareholders unanimously waive it and the company employs no more than 10 full-time employees on annual average.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss accounting law (Code of Obligations, articles 957–963b); unlisted AGs may prepare financial statements under Swiss GAAP, IFRS, or equivalent recognized standards; listed AGs must apply Swiss GAAP FER or IFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: There is no annual UBO confirmation filing in Switzerland. The Register of Members is updated immediately upon each share transfer; the acquiring shareholder must provide documentary proof, and the Board must record the acquisition. For bearer shares, owners holding 25% or more must disclose their identity to the company, but this information is maintained internally and not filed with any public register. The annual tax return records share capital and corporate changes but does not require UBO confirmation. Commercial Register updates for directors or capital changes are event-driven within 14 days, not annual.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 0 if audit waiver applies; USD 4,000 – USD 12,000 for limited audit; USD 15,000 – USD 30,000 for ordinary audit

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 8.5% Swiss federal corporate income tax on net profit after tax (effective federal rate approximately 7.83% pre-tax) plus cantonal and communal taxes resulting in a combined effective rate of approximately 11.5%–21.0% depending on domicile (e.g., Zug ~14.6%, Zurich ~21.0%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Federal: no general tax holiday; cantonal R&D tax super-deductions (120%–150% of qualifying R&D expenditures) available in most cantons; cantonal patent box regime (10%–20% of qualifying IP income); notional interest deduction (NID) for qualifying excess equity; holding company and mixed company regimes abolished in principle but transitional privileges protected until 2025.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Swiss combined federal and cantonal corporate income tax return for legal entities ('Steuererklärung für juristische Personen' / 'Déclaration fiscale pour personnes morales'); filed electronically via the cantonal tax administration's e-filing portal (e.g., Taxat, VAX or ESTV eTax) or in paper form if no electronic access.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Tax return and financial statements of the Aktiengesellschaft (AG) must be filed within 6 months after the fiscal year-end (31 December for calendar-year companies); extension of up to an additional 6 months available upon reasoned request; Swiss Federal Tax Administration may impose final deadlines under the federal tax harmonization rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit per statutory financial statements before tax adjustments, including intangible income from AI subtitle/dubbing licenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident AGs with a Swiss permanent establishment (PE) must apportion income attributable to Swiss operations using arm's length transfer pricing records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Paid-up share capital, reserves, and retained earnings as at balance sheet date; used to compute cantonal capital tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-owned AGs must disclose shareholder loans and capital contributions to avoid hidden equity reclassification.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Field C – Participations and dividend deductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Dividend income from qualified participations (≥10% or voting power) eligible for partial or full participation deduction.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign shareholders claiming treaty benefits must attach Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) and beneficial ownership declaration.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Field D – IP income and research & development expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Separate schedule for patent box or R&D super-deduction calculations; AI algorithm development and post-production tooling may qualify.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents must maintain proper cost accounting and substance documentation to warrant Swiss IP economic ownership.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim for foreign withholding tax credits and reimbursement of Swiss 35% anticipatory tax on gross receipts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Refund applications must use FTA forms 823/823B with TRC and supporting agreements.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers default interest of 3.25% per annum on outstanding tax; procedural fines of CHF 100–10,000 under cantonal and federal tax law; intentional tax evasion subject to fine up to 200% of evaded tax and publication of verdict; refusal to file may result in estimation of tax by assessment notice and criminal proceedings.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% Swiss anticipatory tax on gross dividends paid by an AG; reduced by applicable double taxation agreement (DTA) to 0%–15% for direct and portfolio investors.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim DTA relief on outbound dividends: (i) obtain Tax Residency Certificate (Form 823 A/TH 01) from the beneficial owner's tax authority; (ii) file Swiss request for relief at source (Form 823A) or refund (Form 823B) with the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (FTA); (iii) possess documentary proof of shareholding period (≥6 months or ≥12 months depending on DTA) and beneficial ownership; (iv) attach the subsidy agreement and board minutes approving, the distribution. Direct zero-rate relief is generally available for corporate shareholders holding ≥10% capital in CH AG, subject to substance requirements.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: Swiss domestic law imposes no withholding tax on license fees for the use of IP (including AI software, subtitles, and voice reproductions); DTA treaty rates commonly 0%. Interest: 0% withholding tax on ordinary cross-border intercompany debt interest; a 35% anticipatory tax may arise only on interest from publicly issued borrowings, Swiss bank-issued debentures, or certain profit-sharing loans.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Swiss entities of a multinational group with group annual gross revenues of CHF 50 million or more must prepare a Master File and Local File under the Swiss transfer pricing documentation practice; a Country-by-Country (CbC) Report is mandatory where consolidated group revenue exceeds CHF 900 million. Below the threshold, arm's length documentation must still be available on request to justify intercompany pricing (e.g., AI license fees charged to foreign affiliates).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland does not impose a general Economic Substance Regulation (ESR) regime comparable to UAE; however, treaty eligibility, participation relief, and qualifying IP incentives require real economic substance: substantive premises, qualified staff, management decisions in Switzerland, and active business activity. The Federal Supreme Court and Swiss tax practice deny treaty benefits or privileges to letterbox AGs lacking minimum commercial substance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentional or grossly negligent understatement of generated AI subtitle/dubbing revenue, fraudulent misclassification of Swiss-source licence income to tax haven entities, or omitted capital gains from foreign stock holdings in the AG's tax return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Re-assessment up to 10 years; interest on additional tax; fine up to 200% of evaded tax under Art. 175 DBG (Federal Tax Act); publication of criminal judgments; imprisonment in severe cases under Art. 176 DBG.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false tax returns may be held jointly and severally liable for the AG's unpaid tax, liable for restitution, subject to travel bans and asset seizure, and imprisonment up to 3 years or 5 years if acting for self-enrichment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing a dividend or hidden profit transfer to non-resident shareholders without withholding or remitting the 35% Swiss anticipatory tax; fictitious dividend set-offs via related-party loans.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Anticipatory tax remains due by law; penalty up to 200% of unpaid tax; interest at 3.25% p.a.; criminal sanctions for attempted tax evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and responsible officers are personally liable for the withheld amount; court-ordered personal bankruptcy in fraud cases; restriction on travel and binding administrative compulsory measures.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Absence of valid TP documentation for AI intercompany licensing, artificial margin shifting via aggressive cost-plus allocation, or a Swiss AG lacking personnel and operational premises while claiming IP economic ownership.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fiscal income adjustment to arm's length value; additional cantonal and federal tax plus late interest; denial of DTA treaty relief for outbound subsidiary payments; publication of assessments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for the tax adjustment on hidden profit distributions; travel bans and asset freezing in significant evasion projects; criminal liability where TP manipulation leads to wrongful loss of tax.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using bank accounts of the subtitle/AI studio to process invoicing for non-existent clients, layering through third-party payment rails (Stripe/Wise) to disguise origin of funds, or accepting crypto payments from high-risk countries without proper AML customer due diligence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Art. 305bis Swiss Criminal Code (CC): imprisonment up to 3 years (or 5 years in serious cases) and fine up to CHF 500,000; confiscation of assets; administrative sanctions under FINMA Anti-Money Laundering Ordinance (AMLO) up to CHF 10 million.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal criminal conviction of directors involved; civil liability for investor loss; mandatory travel restrictions and extradition risk; disqualification from serving as director in Switzerland.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company Abuse and Tax Benefit Denial
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a nominal Swiss AG with no employees or premises while describing the AI post-production studio as purely an invoicing platform; claiming privilege of low cantonal rates without actual allocation of personnel, servers, or R&D to Switzerland.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Swiss tax authorities may set aside invoices and re-attribute profit to the beneficial owner; legal liability creates a constructive dividend subject to 35% WHT and additional taxes; treaty benefits denied under Article 29 anti-abuse provisions; company may be struck off in case of abandoned registered office.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal joint liability of board directors; seizure of personal assets; ordering of restitution to tax authorities; travel bans; in aggravated cases imprisonment for tax fraud or falsity in commercial documents.
